NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular business
  hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a recording is
  available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and
  Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received
  before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 8, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR HUFF.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-I AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

  APPROVED.

 F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 27, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER requested that the Peartree Lane expenditures be
broken out into more detailed line-item expenditures within the Budget Amendments. City
Manager Grammer agreed and noted that all expenses related to this emergency are being
carefully tracked.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE - THIRD QUARTER 2023

Erick Quintero, Waste Management Public Sector Services Manager, presented the
following winners of Waste Management’s 3rd quarter Recycling Hero drawing:

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 2249 CARRIAGE DRIVE
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: RED ONION, 736 BART EARLE WAY

Erick Quintero provided a few updates related to the recent reroutes which began July 31,
as well as updates related to the Peartree Lane land movement.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  TASK ORDER FOR TRIPEPI  SMITH  FOR  DISASTER  RESPONSE
  COMMUNICATION SUPPORT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve a Task Order under the Tripepi
  Smith Master Professional Services Agreement for the 2023-24 Fiscal Year for
  communication support for disaster response in an amount not to exceed $50,000;
  and 2) Adjust the Public Information contract services budget in the amount of
  $50,000 to include the added cost of communication support services under the
  currently declared disaster.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR HUFF expressed concern about the proposed task order for $50,000, noting that she
would like to see the funds go towards helping those affected and displaced by the disaster.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated this was a good precautionary measure to have in
place, noting that the City Manager explained there is no expectation to spend much more on
this particular service. COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that our hearts go out to those
affected, and that these particular sources of funds are not appropriate for residents’ relief. She
stated that she supports approving the staff recommendation.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 8, 2023
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN agreed with MAYOR HUFF that the focus should be on
supporting the displaced residents, but also agreed with COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA
about the need for the funds as a precautionary measure. He stated that we need to continue
to be transparent and responsive in providing information.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER shared positive feedback she received from the
community about the communications related to the land movement. She also agreed that
communications are expected to slow as the emergency stabilizes. She also provided
feedback about her positive experience visiting the Local Assistance Center.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

MAYOR HUFF confirmed that the $50,000 task order includes the $26,840 that has already
been spent.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the amount spent was near the City Manager’s
signing limit.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  1) APPROVE A TASK ORDER UNDER THE TRIPEPI SMITH MASTER
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR THE 2023-24 FISCAL YEAR
  FOR COMMUNICATION SUPPORT FOR DISASTER RESPONSE IN AN
  AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $50,000; AND 2) ADJUST THE PUBLIC
  INFORMATION CONTRACT SERVICES BUDGET IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $50,000 TO INCLUDE THE ADDED COST OF COMMUNICATION SUPPORT
  SERVICES UNDER THE CURRENTLY DECLARED DISASTER.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  FOUNDERS PARK PROJECT-REQUEST TO REJECT BID AND CONSIDER
  PROJECT ALTERNATIVES

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Reject the bid from KASA Construction Inc.
  received on July 27, 2023 for Founders Park; and 2) Direct this project back to the Park
  & Activities Commission for further study.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER inquired if Eagle Scouts or other volunteer groups could
help with this project. She agreed with staff’s recommendation to proceed with the landscaping
and address equipment at a later time.

Public Works Director Wahba explained that a significant portion of the revised bid was for
preparing the ground and drainage, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA and
MAYOR HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated he supports rejecting the bid, suggested a phased
approach to complete the project, and echoed the idea of possibly using community volunteers.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 8, 2023
   1) REJECT THE BID FROM KASA CONSTRUCTION INC. RECEIVED ON
  JULY 27, 2023 FOR FOUNDERS PARK; AND 2) DIRECT THIS PROJECT
  BACK TO THE PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION FOR FURTHER STUDY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the July South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Board Meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN announced California Contract Cities Association’s annual
Fall Educational Summit will be held September 8 – 10 in San Diego.

MAYOR HUFF attended the Cal Cities Los Angeles Division’s Installation Dinner, installing
Rolling Hills Council Member Bea Dieringer as the new President.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  APPOINTMENT OF PLANNING COMMISSIONER

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPOINT SHERI REPP-LOADSMAN TO FILL THE ONE VACANCY ON THE
  PLANNING COMMISSION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL-ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:46 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to Tuesday, August 22,
2023, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor
